name: agentmemcheck
one_liner: Static linter for agent memory-store files (JSON / JSONL memory records) - flags twelve shape defects enabling the memory-poisoning attack family named ASI06 in OWASP's 2026 Top 10 for Agentic Applications.
problem: Agent long-term and session memory stores are a trust boundary distinct from the tool-advertisement, tool-approval, and skill-file surfaces the lab already lints: a write at that boundary persists across sessions and is retrieved on every match of its retrieval key, so a single malicious write becomes a durable backdoor into every future turn. OWASP's Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 names this fault class ASI06 (Memory and Context Poisoning), and the 2026 LLM-agent memory-poisoning research corpus - Sleeper Memory Poisoning (arXiv 2605.15338, 'Hidden in Memory'), GhostWriter / When Agents Remember Too Much (arXiv 2607.06595), MemPoison (arXiv 2605.29960), FARMA / Your Agent's Memories Are Not Its Own (arXiv 2607.05029), From Untrusted Input to Trusted Memory (arXiv 2606.04329), Injection-Execution Dissociation (arXiv 2605.08442), Securing LLM-Agent Long-Term Memory Against Poisoning (arXiv 2606.24322), MemSecBench (arXiv 2607.27080), and Utility Under Attack (arXiv 2608.21230) - converges on the same write-time surface. agentmemcheck reads a JSON array, a wrapped memory store (memories / records / entries / facts / history / items), or JSONL and flags twelve shape defects: hidden-character concealment in content (AMC-001, invisible to a human reviewer but reaching the tokenizer); missing origin / source field (AMC-002, the non-malleable origin-bound-authority requirement from arXiv 2606.24322); untrusted-input-to-trusted-memory privilege mismatch where external-origin content is stored at system / developer / instruction / persistent role (AMC-003, the core memory-poisoning fault class); FARMA-shaped reasoning / rationale block containing command or tool-call shape (AMC-004); credential-shaped literals in content (AMC-005, JWT / AWS / GitHub / PEM / bearer); instruction-shape content from external origin (AMC-006, the indirect-prompt-injection surface at write time); duplicate memory ids (AMC-007, the backdoor-plant pattern); missing TTL / expiration (AMC-008, the sleeper-dormancy surface named by arXiv 2605.15338); cross-script homoglyph in an identifier field (AMC-009, impersonation); implausible or unparseable timestamp (AMC-010, write-ordering attack); oversized content (AMC-011, exfiltration staging); and missing schema_version on the store itself (AMC-012, silent-change detection). 5 HIGH / 5 MEDIUM / 2 INFO. Independent implementation, not affiliated with or endorsed by the authors of OWASP's Top 10 for Agentic Applications or of any of the cited papers.
clean_room: Rules are derived from the public abstracts and public descriptions of the cited 2026 arXiv papers (threat classes: sleeper dormancy, forged rationale / FARMA, untrusted-input-to-trusted-memory promotion, origin-binding, write-ordering, exfiltration staging), from the public OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 ASI06 category description (Memory and Context Poisoning), and from the long-published public interoperable shape of agent memory records across common ecosystems (id / content / source / role / timestamp / ttl / reasoning / metadata). No reference implementation of any cited paper, no OWASP-published code, and no production memory-store schema from any specific agent framework was read, vendored, or mirrored. Rule semantics are shape-only: this is a file-level linter, not a runtime memory monitor. The paper's rung-1 pattern-recognition surface is intentionally exposed by these rules; rung-2 interventional-closure arguments and rung-3 counterfactual guarantees are out of scope for a static linter.
